header.title: How to Check a Washing Machine Motor Capacitor
header.description: This guide explains how to diagnose a faulty washing machine motor capacitor using a multimeter. Learn to safely discharge the capacitor and test its functionality to determine if it needs replacement.

steps.description: This step instructs the user to unplug the washing machine, access the motor, and prepare the start capacitor for work.
actions: Unplug your washing machine
Use insulated handles to avoid electric shock
Remove the rear panel
Find the start capacitor
Remove the metal cover
steps.part: Rear panel, Start capacitor, Metal cover

steps.description: Remove the wires from the terminals using needle-nose pliers.
actions: remove wires
use needle-nose pliers

steps.description: Discharge the run capacitor by shorting it out using a screwdriver and jumper wire.
actions: Place one alligator clip from jumper wire to the housing of the capacitor
Place the other alligator clip on the metal shaft of the screwdriver
Put the blade of the screwdriver to one of the terminals
Put the shaft of the screwdriver to the other terminal

steps.description: Calibrate the multimeter by setting it to the ohm scale and adjusting the wheel until the needle reads zero.
actions: Change multimeter to ohm scale
Touch the two lead points to one another
Switch the adjusting wheel until the needle reaches zero, pointing upward

steps.description: This step involves using a multimeter to test a capacitor by observing its needle movement when leads are connected in both polarities.
actions: Touch the black lead to the right capacitor terminal.
Touch the red lead to the left capacitor terminal.
Observe the multimeter needle movement.
Reverse the leads.
Observe the multimeter needle movement.
If the needle doesn't move, replace the capacitor.
